messages:
deploy-bot: AUTOMATION: Release pipeline PAUSED by ops (reason: incident/inc-2026-021 - kvcache OOM in eu-west-1). Candidate pinned to release-2026-03-18-hotfix-1. All scheduled rollouts are held. @ops-oncall please ack.

erika: acked. seeing elevated kvcache eviction + OOM traces in EU canaries. good call to pause.

ben: can we confirm which services are impacted? is this a model runtime issue or infra-level?

ops-oncall: infra-level — gpu nodes in eu-west-1 intermittently hit high memory during long-context requests, appears tied to recent kvcache kernel tweak. Happening on 2/6 canaries. Full runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kvcache-oom

alice: thanks. ops, can we do a quick triage path: 1) pin to previous kvcache-compatible build 2) re-run canaries with bounded seq len 3) if green, resume.

ops-oncall: plan sounds right. I ran a dry command to pin current candidate and block new starts:
```
# pinned by ops
deploybot pin --release release-2026-03-18-hotfix-1 --reason "incident/inc-2026-021 kvcache OOM"
deploybot hold --scope all --until 2026-03-18T05:00:00Z --note "ops triage"
```

carol: for the UI migration rollout scheduled at 03:30 UTC, can we move non-critical changes to the 05:00 window and prioritize the hotfix for immediate canary replay? sales is already pinging about a customer affecting EU cluster.

release-manager: agreed. moving non-customer-facing releases out of the 03:00 window. Hotfix will get zone-first canary at 03:45 in eu-west-1, then staggered to eu-central at 04:15 if green.

david: heads-up: if we shift the change window, we should notify SRE on-call and the APAC schedule owners. Also add a blameless note in the release notes about the temporary pin/rollback path.

ben: do we need a soft rollback of the kvcache kernel change on the clusters? Or can we prefer a model runtime compatibility patch? Ops preference?

ops-oncall: soft rollback is low-touch for now — revert kernel tweak on a small subset of nodes and repeat canary. Preference: revert then push compatibility patch after incident.

erika: I'll draft the customer-facing blurb and update the release notes. Suggested copy: "We paused scheduled rollouts in EU while we investigate increased memory usage affecting long-context requests. A targeted hotfix has been pinned and is under validation."

release-manager: ok to proceed with that copy. ops, target ETA for first canary replay?

ops-oncall: starting revert on eu-west-1 small pool now, expect first canary replay in ~20m. Will post logs.

deploy-bot: NOTE: automatic canary scheduler canceled previous jobs; new canary scheduled: release-2026-03-18-hotfix-1 -> eu-west-1 (canary) at 2270012465.

carol: thx. sales wants a quick heads-up SMS to impacted accounts; @release-manager can you approve?

release-manager: approved. send the short blurb and link to status page.

david: logging action items: 1) ops revert kernel tweak (done on small pool) 2) replay hotfix canary 3) monitor kvcache metrics 4) if stable, unhold and stagger non-critical rollouts 5) update postmortem with root cause and rollout change.

erika: added note to #postmortems later. cc @devex for any SDK release pin instructions.

ops-oncall: canary traffic started. early metrics are promising (memory stable, no OOM spikes). will keep playing additional load tests for the next 30m.

ben: awesome. if green, let's unhold and resume with the pinned hotfix, then schedule a controlled reapply of the kernel tweak on a single availability zone next week.

deploy-bot: UNHOLD scheduled: deploybot unhold --release release-2026-03-18-hotfix-1 --at 2026-03-18T04:15:00Z (auto-unhold disabled if regressions detected).

carol: adding note to the change window calendar: EU window adjusted, non-critical moved to 05:00 UTC.

ops-oncall: final status update in 25m. so far: canary stable.

release-manager: thanks all. will finalize release notes and customer message after 30m validation. :thumbsup:
